title: Shadow Clone
text: Almost on reflex, Ren slashed at Rafumi with his sword, but with a poof, Rafumi turned to smoke and leapt a short distance away.
“Being all coy and not telling me…”
“It’s a joke I learned from Shield Hero in the future world.”
“Wait, that’s me? …Then is it a callback to something a professor said back in my original world?”
“Raph, raph, raph, raph, raph… An attack from an immature Azott like that could never land on me.”
Rafumi said something along those lines, flashing a fearless grin as she taunted Ren.
“Don’t mess with me! Tell me!”
“Relying on knowledge for absolutely everything isn’t good, Azott. Besides, I’m not the kind of golem who does something as boring as dropping spoilers in a place like this.”
“Please, isn’t there any way to return Ren-sama to normal!? Tell us, please!”
“That isn’t my mission. Whether I answer is entirely up to my own judgment, and since telling you wouldn’t be any fun, I won’t.”
Rafumi’s reaction was unexpected. I’d figured she’d immediately confess to being the culprit, but apparently not.
“What’s the point of teasing me!”

Poof! Poof! Rafumi dodged every single one of Ren’s slashing attacks using her clones, indeed. Each time, she followed up with a provocative little dance. Extremely, aggressively annoying. To think you’d pull something like that on your own creator.

“Relax. If it were truly something dangerous, I’d intervene. This isn’t dangerous, and I simply won’t help because I think it’ll do you good to wake up a little. The time will come when you understand. All’s well that ends well.”
“It is not well! What kind of nerve do you have, refusing to obey orders when you were supposedly made by my future self!”
“True enough… It does seem odd that she was apparently sent from the future as an assassin against Kuro-chan, and yet won’t follow Ren’s orders… hmm.”
Whatever the case, Rafumi seemed to be taking something close to a bystander’s stance.
“Motoyasu-kun, don’t you have anything to add?”

Father was fishing for information again, for what must’ve been the umpteenth time. Well, it would be strange for Rafumi to know something I didn’t, I suppose. But I kept quiet. In times like this, one should only answer what one can answer, indeed.
“It’s the inult version of Ren, I say. I think it would be best to introduce him to Luna-chan.”
“Wow… you really don’t waver, do you. Though I guess if Luna-chan, who dotes on Keel-kun so much, saw him, she probably would jump right on him.”
“There’s another one like Kuro out there!? Just how many of these things do you people keep!”
I still intend to raise plenty more Filolial-samas, I say!
“Hmm… Azott, it isn’t as though I merely want to play around either. I won’t spoil anything, but I do intend to lend a hand.”
“What are you planning to do?”
“Kurotarou… no, Kuro, was it. I suppose I could at least act as a playmate for this dejected fellow. Don’t worry. Hup!”
And with that, Rafumi did a spinning leap, and with a poof… transformed into an exact copy of Ren. Well, not quite exact—her features were slightly more idealized.
“Heh… the Dark Swordsman, Shadow Saint… has arrived.”
Inult Ren stood there with his mouth hanging open, staring at this Rafumi-turned-Ren.
“Wow…”

“Kuro—no, Fang of Pitch-Black Darkness. How long will you stand there dazed? To crush the wicked Holy Goddess, Pidesmachinar, who schemes to bring about the Prophecy of Catastrophe, we must confront the Dark Destiny! Do not fall behind!”
She said this in a tone mimicking Awakened Ren, bending her fingers into an odd shape and hiding half her face.
“Ohh! A new page is carved into the Chronicle of the Dark Holy Hero, the Dark Brave!”
Kuro-chan struck a pose along with her, looking thoroughly delighted.

“You two, join in as well. As the Shadow Clone of Azott, the Alchemy Sword, who has become a pampered lapdog, I shall play the part of the Dark Holy Hero. We shall act as the Dark Holy Knights, and overcome the fate of ruin.”
“Eh? Ah, y-yes.”

“First, as for our future course of action—judging from your Levels, this area should serve well as a hunting ground. We’ll take on jobs at a moderate pace, and once your Levels have risen sufficiently, we’ll go together to defeat the next prey.”
“I—indeed, this reaction is unmistakably Ren-sama.”
“With this, we should be able to manage even without Ren-sama present.”

Everyone seemed unsure how to react at first, but since the appearance was such a perfect match for Ren, his companions gradually joined into the conversation. Amid all the enthusiastic back-and-forth, she seemed fully capable of commanding Kuro-chan and the others with the same crisp switch of tone Ren normally used even while playing Awakened Ren. Well, I suppose that makes sense, given she was created by Ren—she probably comes equipped with a fair amount of the game knowledge Ren possesses. And as this Rafumi, an exact copy of himself, took command while Kuro-chan happily played along, the real Ren—now in his inult form—watched on with dull, lusterless eyes. Was this the moment right before he snapped back to his senses and got angry? Thankfully, he seemed to have forgotten all about the mystery of how he ended up in this inult form.
“R-Ren looks like a cat whose brain just got wrecked…”
According to Father, there’s apparently a video of a cat that looks like it just walked in on something resembling infidelity. Ren, apparently, was giving off that exact same vibe.
“There, there… okay, it’s alright. Staring at it too long is bad for your eyes, so let’s not look, okay? It’s okay, see?”
Father, unable to help himself, scooped up the dazed, blank-eyed Ren and gently stroked his head. At that, Ren snapped back to his senses and started thrashing.
“Don’t pity me and try to comfort me!”
Ren, putting up as much resistance as he could muster, shoved his paw pad into Father’s cheek and was finally released, landing on the ground.
“That was a completely animal way of comforting someone!”

“Oops, my bad. So, Ren, what do you want to do now? Seems like Rafumi-chan is willing to act as your stand-in, take care of Kuro-chan who’s feeling down, and even handle giving orders to your companions in your place, though.”

His whole position had been completely usurped. If Rafumi kept handling Kuro-chan and Ren’s companions like this, would that finally free me up to embrace Filo-tan? Incidentally, it did not. Even though she was supposed to be acting as Ren’s stand-in, the moment I lunged for a hug, a cloned Rafumi swapped in with a cheerful “Too bad! It’s me!” instead. Gah… Rafumi being able to split into clones makes her endlessly troublesome, I say.

“You did say you’re not fond of groups, so should we just carry on as usual—prepare for the Waves in that form? Or, since it seems like it’d be rough, do you want to come stay with us? I’m happy to talk it over. As a merchant, I can quietly gather information behind the scenes, and it sounded like Ren’s companions were planning to go hear the country’s side of things too.”
“We need to find a way to turn you back, after all.”
Ren seemed to be hesitating over how to answer.
“Sorry, but no matter what, I have to get back to my original form, so I’m going to go look into—”
Just as Ren seemed about to refuse, Luna-chan came clomping over, carrying Keel. Right, Keel had come over here today. She’d been doing circus training over at Elephant and Panda’s place, hadn’t she?
“What’s up, big bros? Hm? Who’s that kid?”
“Ah, Keel-kun, Luna-chan. Um, I’m not sure if the timing here is good or bad, but…”
Father glanced back and forth between Keel and Ren. They really did look remarkably alike. Incidentally, Ren, in his inult form, had nothing on but a light wrap of cloth around his body.
“Doesn’t he kinda look like me?”
“He does not!”

“Ah… explaining the situation’s gonna get complicated, but this kid—no, he, is Ren. Actually the Sword Hero. A few days ago, someone apparently attacked him out of nowhere, and for some reason he ended up in this form now—”

Just as she was explaining, Luna-chan took a big step forward and stared intently at Ren. Yikes… that presence really is something to fear. Still, it was considerably weaker than that time before. No doubt that was thanks to Keel being here. To begin with, Luna-chan turns into a perfectly docile Filolial-sama as long as Keel is around.
“Wow… he looks a lot like Keel-kun. Keel-kun, cute.”
“Not cute. Cool, right? That guy over there with the sword.”
“Coo—”
If Ren had answered that he wasn’t cool, it would’ve meant picking a fight with Keel, which would naturally come right back around to bite him—so Ren seemed to choke on his words.
“Amazing. For him to resemble Keel-kun this much… could he be a bridegroom?”
“Not a bridegroom! I’m a guy!”
Incidentally, everyone around had already been thoroughly informed that Keel is female. And yet, as always, Keel kept insisting he was male.
